deities: Naina Devi (form of Parvati/Durga, as two eyes)

history.dynasty: No dynasty documented; Kumaoni tradition claims ancient (Katyuri/Chand-era) origins
history.summary: Identity confirmed: the famous Naina Devi Shakti Peeth of Nainital on the north bank of Naini Lake, distinct from the Naina Devi temple at Bilaspur, Himachal Pradesh (seq 1588, id naina-devi-temple). One of the 51 Shakti Peeths: Sati's eyes (naina) are believed to have fallen here, and the town of Nainital itself is named after the goddess. Tradition traces the shrine to at least the 15th century; Moti Lal Shah installed the Naina Devi idol in 1842; the temple was destroyed in the great landslide of 1880 and rebuilt by locals in 1883. The sanctum holds two eyes as the central deity, flanked by Kali and Ganesha; a Hanuman shrine and a sacred peepal tree stand in the courtyard. Nanda Ashtami is the grandest annual festival.

name: Naina Devi Temple
town_description: Nainital is a hill-station town in the Kumaon Himalayas at about 2,000 m, built around the mango-shaped Naini Lake. It is a major summer resort and pilgrimage town; the lake, Mall Road (Mallital/Tallital) and the Naina Devi temple on the lake's northern bank are its anchors.

travel.road: In the heart of Nainital town on the northern bank of Naini Lake (Mallital side); ~2 km from Tallital bus stand, walkable from Mall Road

visitor_information.best_time: March-June and September-November; Nanda Ashtami (August/September) and Navratri are the grandest but most crowded periods
